correctness.rationale: For all integer n>=2 and q>=1, convolution differentiation and a sign input attain exactly the normalized total variation of the powered Fejer kernel. Strict logarithmic concavity in each complete noncentral nodal lobe yields a unique stationary maximum satisfying n*cot(nu)=cot(u), with explicit peak M_{n,k}; central/side and odd-terminal variations give the exact finite numerator. Parseval gives Z=n^{-q} sum_j c_j^2. For fixed q, t=2u/n rescaling gives the sinc^{2q} integral, stationary roots tan r=r and summable k^{-2q} lobe envelope. For high q, write H_n=F_n/n and expand log H_n(t)=-(n^2-1)t^2/12+O(n^4 t^4) uniformly near zero, yielding a uniform Laplace mass sqrt(12*pi/[q(n^2-1)]). A uniform <1 gap off the center plus the tail envelope makes all other lobes O(4^{-q}) in total variation; the resulting norm is sqrt(q(n^2-1)/(3*pi)) uniformly n>=2. Boundary cases n=2, odd n and q=1 included; real and complex L∞ sign attainment are both valid. The independent numerical tests are supporting checks only; no finite test establishes a quantified limit.
